statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 16 while Stress stays elevated at 54; the Nasdaq-100 enters the August monthly expiry close having retraced both of today's extremes, with the long end near 20-month yield highs.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with functioning mean reversion: the session has produced a full round trip, both extremes have been retraced, price sits mid-range in cash and futures, and implied volatility is at session lows. A narrow evidence-based caution window is carried at 19:00Z-20:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow into the cash close, and it releases at that close. Tail remains well below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Inside the expiry close: the Nasdaq-100 has retraced both of today's extremes and sits below its open, with VIX at session lows against a 4.74% 10-year.
body:
Cash NDX trades near 29,317.76, about +0.36% on the day against a 29,213.17 previous close. The index opened at 29,359.60, was sold to a 29,142.44 low, reclaimed the entire decline to a 29,405.12 high and has since handed back roughly ninety points to trade below its own open; NQ September futures are near 29,387.75, about +0.30%, inside a 29,220.00-29,539.00 range against a 29,300.50 prior close and some 151 points beneath their session high. That sequence remains the central Tail evidence and it points the same way it has all afternoon. Both extremes have been retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and price sits in the middle of its range rather than pinned at an edge, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that overwhelms mean reversion. Volatility agrees: VIX is 14.89, down 6.00% on the day and near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range.

The one genuinely hour-specific condition is mechanical. This is the August monthly options expiry, and the assessment hour running to the 20:00Z cash close is when expiring index and single-stock open interest is settled and rolled. That concentrates order flow into a shrinking window and is a real, if bounded, mechanism for a fast directional push that does not immediately retrace. It is the reason Tail is carried at 16 rather than the 13 published for each of the three preceding hours. It is not evidence of a pathological path: nothing observed so far in this hour shows one-way structure, and the elevation is scheduled-flow risk that releases at the close.

The stress side of the ledger stays genuinely elevated and is almost entirely a rates and energy story. The 10-year is 4.74%, up about three and a half basis points, the 30-year is 5.28%, and the long end has given back close to all of the ground it recovered after the Treasury expanded its long-dated buyback operations earlier in the week; the 2-year at 4.24% is the firmest part of the curve on the day. Energy carries the other half: WTI is roughly $86.83 and Brent $94.07, essentially flat on the session but heading for a second consecutive weekly gain of around five percent as the Strait of Hormuz disruption stays unresolved. Neither of those is transmitting into equity price structure right now, but both are why a large recoverable drawdown remains plausible.

Internals are split rather than aligned, which is the classic profile for a mixed dominant mode. Delayed latest-session context shows five of eight megacaps higher with dispersion near 1.9 percentage points, led by Tesla and Alphabet while Nvidia and Apple are lower, and the semiconductor complex averages about -0.7% with ARM and Intel the largest drags. Sector breadth is positive but narrow: communication services and consumer cyclicals near one percent, technology up only about a tenth. Cross-asset futures context is similarly two-sided, with the Dow outperforming the Nasdaq, VIX futures lower, gold up about 2.4% and Treasury futures lower across the curve. Strong aligned breadth would be needed to amplify Tail, and it is not present.

Confidence is held at 88. Current index and futures levels, the day range, VIX, the full Treasury curve, both crude benchmarks, the already-released flash PMI set and the forward calendar were all verified directly at this cutoff, and the delayed cross-asset context is used only as confirmation. The horizon beyond 21:00Z is a different problem: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so every later slot in the published forecast describes a market with no tradable price path, and the scores there step to background floors while confidence decays with distance from the last observed print.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: twelve hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z through 18:00Z) while the remaining twelve clock-hours, covering the August 20 US afternoon and evening plus scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours the published Tail held a narrow 12-16 band and the mapped policy state was green throughout. The shape is informative: Tail sat at 12 through the Asian and European hours with Stress easing from 59 to 54 as the overnight tape stayed orderly, then stepped up to 15-16 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z flash-PMI and US-open window, where the dominant mode was briefly published as event/whipsaw. Since that release Tail has come back down through 14 to 13 and held there for four consecutive hours while the mode returned to mixed, which is exactly the decay profile a cleanly absorbed event produces. Stress eased in step, from 58 at the release to 53 in the most recent hour, while Confidence climbed steadily from 83 to 88 as more of the session's evidence became directly observable. No hour in the window reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: The forecast carries the current hour at Tail 16, one notch above the preceding three hours, purely for the concentrated August monthly expiry flow that settles into the 20:00Z cash close; that elevation is a scheduled-flow checkpoint rather than an observed structure and it releases immediately afterwards, with the 20:00Z slot stepping back to 11 as only the thin futures tail remains. From 21:00Z the published horizon changes character entirely: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so every subsequent slot describes a market with no tradable price path. Tail falls to a floor of 4-6 there because the pathological path this score measures requires a live market, and Stress steps down to 35-40, a level that represents the standing rate and energy backdrop, a 5.28% 30-year and Brent near $94, rather than any live condition. Confidence decays gradually across the weekend from 88 to 64 with distance from the last observed print rather than because evidence has been contradicted. The dominant mode is published as normal from the close onward, since a halted market has no structure to characterise, and no scheduled US macro event falls inside the window: the next checkpoints are Monday's Chicago Fed index and then Wednesday's PCE and NVIDIA results, both beyond this horizon.
